sanskrit: upāsya rātriśeṣaṃ tu śoṇākūle maharṣibhiḥ niśāyāṃ suprabhātāyāṃ viśvāmitro 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having passed the remainder of the night on the bank of the Śoṇā along with the great seers, when the night had turned into a fair dawn, Viśvāmitra spoke.

sanskrit: suprabhātā niśā rāma pūrvā saṃdhyā pravartate uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te gamanāyābhirocaya
english: "The night has brightened beautifully, Rāma; the morning twilight is beginning. Rise, rise — good fortune to you — make ready for the journey."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtvā paurvāhṇikīṃ kriyām gamanaṃ rocayām āsa vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: Hearing his words and performing the morning rites, Rāma resolved to set out and then spoke these words.

sanskrit: ayaṃ śoṇaḥ śubhajalo gādhaḥ pulinamaṇḍitaḥ katareṇa pathā brahman saṃtariṣyāmahe vayam
english: "Here is the Śoṇā, its waters pure, its ford shallow, adorned with sandbanks. By which path, O brahmin, shall we cross it?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa viśvāmitro 'bravīd idam eṣa panthā mayoddiṣṭo yena yānti maharṣayaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Viśvāmitra replied: "This is the path I have pointed out — the very one by which the great seers travel."

sanskrit: te gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ gate 'rdhadivase tadā jāhnavīṃ saritāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ dadṛśur munisevitām
english: Travelling a great distance, when midday had passed, they beheld the Jāhnavī, best of rivers, frequented by sages.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇyasalilāṃ haṃsasārasasevitām babhūvur muditāḥ sarve munayaḥ saharāghavāḥ tasyās tīre tataś cakrus te āvāsaparigraham
english: Seeing her sacred waters thronged with swans and cranes, all the sages together with Rāghava were filled with joy, and they took up their lodging on her bank.

sanskrit: tataḥ snātvā yathānyāyaṃ saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ hutvā caivāgnihotrāṇi prāśya cāmṛtavad dhaviḥ
english: Then, having bathed according to rule, having satisfied the ancestral spirits and the gods, having offered oblations into the sacred fires and partaken of the sacrificial food as though it were nectar,

sanskrit: viviśur jāhnavītīre śucau muditamānasāḥ viśvāmitraṃ mahātmānaṃ parivārya samantataḥ
english: They entered a pure spot on the bank of the Jāhnavī with gladdened hearts, surrounding the great-souled Viśvāmitra on all sides.

sanskrit: saṃprahṛṣṭamanā rāmo viśvāmitram athābravīt bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm trailokyaṃ katham ākramya gatā nadanadīpatim
english: With a delighted mind, Rāma then addressed Viśvāmitra: "Revered one, I wish to hear about Gaṅgā, who flows through three paths — how did she, traversing the three worlds, reach the lord of rivers and streams?"

sanskrit: codito rāma vākyena viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ vṛddhiṃ janma ca gaṅgāyā vaktum evopacakrame
english: Prompted by Rāma's words, the great sage Viśvāmitra began to recount the origin and the growth of Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: śailendro himavān nāma dhātūnām ākaro mahān tasya kanyā dvayaṃ rāma rūpeṇāpratimaṃ bhuvi
english: "There is a king of mountains named Himavān, a great treasury of minerals. He had two daughters, Rāma, of unrivalled beauty in the world.

sanskrit: yā meruduhitā rāma tayor mātā sumadhyamā nāmnā menā manojñā vai patnī himavataḥ priyā
english: She who was born of Meru, of slender waist, charming in name and form — Menā — was the mother of both; the beloved wife of Himavat.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ gaṅgeyam abhavaj jyeṣṭhā himavataḥ sutā umā nāma dvitīyābhūt kanyā tasyaiva rāghava
english: Upon her was born Gaṅgā, the elder daughter of Himavat; and a second daughter of his, named Umā, came to be, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: atha jyeṣṭhāṃ surāḥ sarve devatārthacikīrṣayā śailendraṃ varayām āsur gaṅgāṃ tripathagāṃ nadīm
english: Then all the gods, wishing to accomplish the purpose of the deities, petitioned the lord of mountains for the elder daughter — Gaṅgā who flows through three paths.

sanskrit: dadau dharmeṇa himavāṃs tanayāṃ lokapāvanīm svacchandapathagāṃ gaṅgāṃ trailokyahitakāmyayā
english: Himavān, by the law of righteousness and for the good of the three worlds, gave away his daughter Gaṅgā — purifier of all worlds, free to course wherever she wills.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya trilokārthaṃ trilokahitakāriṇaḥ gaṅgām ādāya te 'gacchan kṛtārthenāntarātmanā
english: Receiving her for the benefit of the three worlds, those who promote the welfare of the three worlds departed, taking Gaṅgā with them, their inner selves fulfilled.

sanskrit: yā cānyā śailaduhitā kanyāsīd raghunandana ugraṃ sā vratam āsthāya tapas tepe tapodhanā
english: The other daughter of the mountain king, O joy of the Raghus, having undertaken a fierce vow, performed austerities, she whose wealth was asceticism.

sanskrit: ugreṇa tapasā yuktāṃ dadau śailavaraḥ sutām rudrāyāpratirūpāya umāṃ lokanamaskṛtām
english: On account of her fierce austerities, the best of mountains gave his daughter Umā — honoured by all the worlds — to Rudra, who was without equal.

sanskrit: ete te śaila rājasya sute lokanamaskṛte gaṅgā ca saritāṃ śreṣṭhā umā devī ca rāghava
english: These, then, are the two daughters of the mountain king, both revered by the worlds: Gaṅgā, best of rivers, and the goddess Umā, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: etat te dharmam ākhyātaṃ yathā tripathagā nadī khaṃ gatā prathamaṃ tāta gatiṃ gatimatāṃ vara
english: This righteous account has been told to you — how the river Tripathagā first ascended to the sky, O dear one, you who are the best among those who move."

sanskrit: ukta vākye munau tasminn ubhau rāghavalakṣmaṇau pratinandya kathāṃ vīrāv ūcatur munipuṃgavam
english: When the sage had finished speaking, both heroes Rāghava and Lakṣmaṇa, expressing their appreciation of the narrative, addressed the foremost of sages.

sanskrit: dharmayuktam idaṃ brahman kathitaṃ paramaṃ tvayā duhituḥ śailarājasya jyeṣṭhāya vaktum arhasi
english: "What you have told, O brahmin, is supremely righteous. Now it is fitting for you to speak of the elder daughter of the mountain king —

sanskrit: vistaraṃ vistarajño 'si divyamānuṣasaṃbhavam trīn patho hetunā kena pāvayel lokapāvanī
english: — in full detail, for you know how to expand a tale: her birth among gods and men, and by what cause she, the purifier of worlds, purifies the three paths."

sanskrit: kathaṃ gaṅgāṃ tripathagā viśrutā sariduttamā triṣu lokeṣu dharmajña karmabhiḥ kaiḥ samanvitā
english: "How is Gaṅgā, the renowned Tripathagā, best of rivers — endowed with what deeds does she flow through the three worlds, O knower of righteousness?"

sanskrit: tathā bruvati kākutsthe viśvāmitras tapodhanaḥ nikhilena kathāṃ sarvām ṛṣimadhye nyavedayat
english: As the descendant of Kakutstha spoke thus, Viśvāmitra, whose wealth is austerity, narrated the entire tale in full in the midst of the sages.

sanskrit: purā rāma kṛtodvāhaḥ śitikaṇṭho mahātapāḥ dṛṣṭvā ca spṛhayā devīṃ maithunāyopacakrame
english: "Long ago, Rāma, Śitikaṇṭha — the blue-throated one — of great austerity, having married, and gazing upon the goddess with desire, approached her for conjugal union.

sanskrit: śitikaṇṭhasya devasya divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ gatam na cāpi tanayo rāma tasyām āsīt paraṃtapa
english: A divine hundred years passed for the god Śitikaṇṭha, yet still no son was born to him by her, O scorcher of foes, Rāma.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ samudvignāḥ pitāmahapurogamāḥ yad ihotpadyate bhūtaṃ kas tat pratisahiṣyate
english: Then the gods became deeply anxious, led by the Pitāmaha: 'Whatever being is born here — who will be able to bear it?'

sanskrit: abhigamya surāḥ sarve praṇipatyedam abruvan devadeva mahādeva lokasyāsya hite rata surāṇāṃ praṇipātena prasādaṃ kartum arhasi
english: All the gods approached and, bowing low, spoke thus: 'O god of gods, O Mahādeva, you who are devoted to the welfare of this world — in response to the prostration of the gods, be gracious.'

sanskrit: na lokā dhārayiṣyanti tava tejaḥ surottama brāhmeṇa tapasā yukto devyā saha tapaś cara
english: 'The worlds will not be able to bear your seed, O best of gods. United with your brahmic austerity, practise asceticism together with the goddess.'

sanskrit: trailokyahitakāmārthaṃ tejas tejasi dhāraya rakṣa sarvān imāṃl lokān nālokaṃ kartum arhasi
english: 'For the welfare of the three worlds, restrain your vital seed within your own energy. Protect all these worlds; it is not fitting that you render the worlds void.'

sanskrit: devatānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ bāḍham ity abravīt sarvān punaś cedam uvāca ha
english: Having heard the words of the gods, the great lord of all worlds said 'So be it' to all of them, and then spoke again thus:

sanskrit: dhārayiṣyāmy ahaṃ tejas tejasy eva sahomayā tridaśāḥ pṛthivī caiva nirvāṇam adhigacchatu
english: 'I shall restrain my seed within my own energy, together with Umā. Let the thirty gods and the earth attain peace.'

sanskrit: yad idaṃ kṣubhitaṃ sthānān mama tejo hy anuttamam dhārayiṣyati kas tan me bruvantu surasattamāḥ
english: 'But as for this unsurpassed seed of mine that has already been displaced — who shall bear it? Let the best of gods tell me.'

sanskrit: evam uktās tato devāḥ pratyūcur vṛṣabhadhvajam yat tejaḥ kṣubhitaṃ hy etat tad dharā dhārayiṣyati
english: Thus addressed, the gods replied to the one whose banner bears the bull: 'This seed that has been displaced — the Earth shall bear it.'

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ surapatiḥ pramumoca mahītale tejasā pṛthivī yena vyāptā sagirikānanā
english: Thus addressed, the lord of the gods released it upon the surface of the earth, by whose energy the earth with its mountains and forests was pervaded.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ punar idam ūcuś cātha hutāśanam praviśa tvaṃ mahātejo raudraṃ vāyusamanvitaḥ
english: Then the gods again spoke to Hutāśana, the fire: 'Enter into it, O great blazing one — that which belongs to Rudra — accompanied by Vāyu.'

sanskrit: tad agninā punar vyāptaṃ saṃjātaḥ śvetaparvataḥ divyaṃ śaravaṇaṃ caiva pāvakādityasaṃnibham yatra jāto mahātejāḥ kārtikeyo 'gnisaṃbhavaḥ
english: That which was pervaded again by fire became the White Mountain, and a divine thicket of reeds blazing like fire and sun — in that place was born the great-resplendent Kārttikeya, sprung from Agni.

sanskrit: athomāṃ ca śivaṃ caiva devāḥ sarṣi gaṇās tadā pūjayām āsur atyarthaṃ suprītamanasas tataḥ
english: Then the gods together with the hosts of sages, their minds exceedingly well pleased, worshipped both Umā and Śiva with great devotion.

sanskrit: atha śaila sutā rāma tridaśān idam abravīt samanyur aśapat sarvān krodhasaṃraktalocanā
english: Then the daughter of the mountain, Rāma, with eyes reddened in anger, wrathfully cursed all the thirty gods:

sanskrit: yasmān nivāritā caiva saṃgatā putrakāmyayā apatyaṃ sveṣu dāreṣu notpādayitum arhatha adya prabhṛti yuṣmākam aprajāḥ santu patnayaḥ
english: 'Because I was prevented, when united with my husband for the desire of a son — henceforth none of you shall be fit to beget offspring upon your own wives; from this day your wives shall be without children.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā surān sarvāñ śaśāpa pṛthivīm api avane naikarūpā tvaṃ bahubhāryā bhaviṣyasi
english: Having spoken thus and cursed all the gods, she cursed the Earth as well: 'You on the ground, taking manifold forms, shall have many consorts —'

sanskrit: na ca putrakṛtāṃ prītiṃ matkrodhakaluṣī kṛtā prāpsyasi tvaṃ sudurmedhe mama putram anicchatī
english: '— and you, utterly foolish one, defiled by my wrath, who did not desire my son, shall never attain the joy that comes from a son of one's own.'

sanskrit: tān sarvān vrīḍitān dṛṣṭvā surān surapatis tadā gamanāyopacakrāma diśaṃ varuṇapālitām
english: Seeing all the gods abashed, the lord of gods then prepared to depart to the quarter guarded by Varuṇa.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tapa ātiṣṭhat pārśve tasyottare gireḥ himavatprabhave śṛṅge saha devyā maheśvaraḥ
english: Going there, Maheśvara took up austerities on the northern flank of that mountain, on a peak where Himavat has his origin, together with the goddess.

sanskrit: eṣa te vistaro rāma śailaputryā niveditaḥ gaṅgāyāḥ prabhavaṃ caiva śṛṇu me sahalakṣmaṇaḥ
english: This, Rāma, is the full account of the daughter of the mountain that has been set forth for you. Now hear from me, together with Lakṣmaṇa, the origin of Gaṅgā."

sanskrit: tapyamāne tapo deve devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā senāpatim abhīpsantaḥ pitāmaham upāgaman
english: Long ago, while the god was engaged in austerity, the gods together with the hosts of sages, desiring a commander of the divine army, approached the Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: tato 'bruvan surāḥ sarve bhagavantaṃ pitāmaham praṇipatya śubhaṃ vākyaṃ sendrāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ
english: Then all the gods, led by Indra and preceded by Agni, having bowed down before the venerable Pitāmaha, spoke these auspicious words:

sanskrit: yo naḥ senāpatir deva datto bhagavatā purā sa tapaḥ param āsthāya tapyate sma sahomayā
english: 'He who was given to us as commander of the army by the Blessed One long ago — he is engaged in the highest austerity together with Umā.'

sanskrit: yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā saṃvidhatsva vidhānajña tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: 'Whatever must therefore be done next for the welfare of the worlds — arrange it, O knower of sacred ordinance, for you are our highest refuge.'

sanskrit: devatānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ sāntvayan madhurair vākyais tridaśān idam abravīt
english: Having heard the words of the gods, the grandfather of all worlds, soothing the thirty gods with gentle words, spoke thus:

sanskrit: śailaputryā yad uktaṃ tan na prajāsyatha patniṣu tasyā vacanam akliṣṭaṃ satyam eva na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'What has been declared by the daughter of the mountain — that you shall have no progeny from your wives — that utterance of hers, unimpeded, is true; there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: iyam ākāśagā gaṅgā yasyāṃ putraṃ hutāśanaḥ janayiṣyati devānāṃ senāpatim ariṃdamam
english: 'This Gaṅgā who traverses the sky — in her, Hutāśana shall beget a son who will be the subduer of enemies and commander of the army of the gods.'

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhā śailendraduhitā mānayiṣyati taṃ sutam umāyās tad bahumataṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'The elder daughter of the lord of mountains shall honour that son; and this will be greatly approved of by Umā — there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya kṛtārthā raghunandana praṇipatya surāḥ sarve pitāmaham apūjayan
english: Hearing his words, their purpose accomplished, O joy of the Raghus, all the gods bowed down and worshipped the Pitāmaha.

sanskrit: te gatvā parvataṃ rāma kailāsaṃ dhātumaṇḍitam agniṃ niyojayām āsuḥ putrārthaṃ sarvadevatāḥ
english: Going then, Rāma, to Mount Kailāsa adorned with minerals, all the gods commissioned Agni for the purpose of obtaining a son.

sanskrit: devakāryam idaṃ deva samādhatsva hutāśana śailaputryāṃ mahātejo gaṅgāyāṃ teja utsṛja
english: 'Accomplish this divine purpose, O Hutāśana; O great blazing one, discharge your seed into Gaṅgā, daughter of the mountain.'

sanskrit: devatānāṃ pratijñāya gaṅgām abhyetya pāvakaḥ garbhaṃ dhāraya vai devi devatānām idaṃ priyam
english: Having assented to the gods, Pāvaka approached Gaṅgā: 'Bear this embryo, O goddess — this is the wish of the gods.'

sanskrit: ity etad vacanaṃ śrutvā divyaṃ rūpam adhārayat sa tasyā mahimāṃ dṛṣṭvā samantād avakīryata
english: Hearing these words, she assumed a divine form; and seeing her greatness, he shed his seed all around.

sanskrit: samantatas tadā devīm abhyaṣiñcata pāvakaḥ sarvasrotāṃsi pūrṇāni gaṅgāyā raghunandana
english: Then Pāvaka anointed the goddess on all sides, filling all the streams of Gaṅgā, O joy of the Raghus.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tato gaṅgā sarvadevapurohitam aśaktā dhāraṇe deva tava tejaḥ samuddhatam dahyamānāgninā tena saṃpravyathitacetanā
english: Then Gaṅgā spoke to him, the priest of all the gods: 'I am unable to bear your uplifted energy, O god; burned by that fire, my senses are sorely distressed.'

sanskrit: athābravīd idaṃ gaṅgāṃ sarvadevahutāśanaḥ iha haimavate pāde garbho 'yaṃ saṃniveśyatām
english: Then the fire, the oblation-receiver of all gods, said to Gaṅgā: 'Let this embryo be deposited here at the foot of the Himālayas.'

sanskrit: śrutvā tv agnivaco gaṅgā taṃ garbham atibhāsvaram utsasarja mahātejāḥ srotobhyo hi tadānagha
english: Hearing the words of Agni, Gaṅgā — of great splendour — thereupon discharged that exceedingly brilliant embryo from her streams, O sinless one.

sanskrit: yad asyā nirgataṃ tasmāt taptajāmbūnadaprabham kāñcanaṃ dharaṇīṃ prāptaṃ hiraṇyam amalaṃ śubham
english: That which issued forth from her — gleaming like heated Jāmbūnada gold — when it reached the earth became pure, auspicious golden ore.

sanskrit: tāmraṃ kārṣṇāyasaṃ caiva taikṣṇyād evābhijāyata malaṃ tasyābhavat tatra trapusīsakam eva ca
english: From its very sharpness of heat, copper and black iron were born; and its dross there became tin and lead.

sanskrit: tad etad dharaṇīṃ prāpya nānādhātur avardhata
english: That substance, reaching the earth, multiplied into various ores.

sanskrit: nikṣiptamātre garbhe tu tejobhir abhirañjitam sarvaṃ parvatasaṃnaddhaṃ sauvarṇam abhavad vanam
english: The moment the embryo was deposited, the entire forest clinging to the mountains, suffused with those energies, became golden.

sanskrit: jātarūpam iti khyātaṃ tadā prabhṛti rāghava suvarṇaṃ puruṣavyāghra hutāśanasamaprabham
english: From that time onward, O Rāghava, O tiger among men, gold has been known as jātarūpa — blazing equal to Hutāśana.

sanskrit: taṃ kumāraṃ tato jātaṃ sendrāḥ sahamarudgaṇāḥ kṣīrasaṃbhāvanārthāya kṛttikāḥ samayojayan
english: Then, when the boy was born, Indra together with the hosts of Maruts appointed the Kṛttikā stars to nourish him with milk.

sanskrit: tāḥ kṣīraṃ jātamātrasya kṛtvā samayam uttamam daduḥ putro 'yam asmākaṃ sarvāsām iti niścitāḥ
english: They, making a solemn compact, gave milk immediately upon his birth, resolved: 'This boy is the son of all of us.'

sanskrit: tatas tu devatāḥ sarvāḥ kārtikeya iti bruvan putras trailokya vikhyāto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: Then all the gods declared: 'He shall be called Kārttikeya; he shall be the son renowned throughout the three worlds — there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā skannaṃ garbhaparisrave snāpayan parayā lakṣmyā dīpyamānam ivānalam
english: Hearing those words of theirs, they bathed with supreme splendour the one who had been born from the outflow of the womb, blazing like a fire.

sanskrit: skanda ity abruvan devāḥ skannaṃ garbhaparisravāt kārtikeyaṃ mahābhāgaṃ kākutsthajvalanopamam
english: The gods called him Skanda — 'the one who flowed forth' — born from the outflow of the womb: Kārttikeya of great fortune, comparable to the fire of the Kākutsthas.

sanskrit: prādurbhūtaṃ tataḥ kṣīraṃ kṛttikānām anuttamam ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaḍānano bhūtvā jagrāha stanajaṃ payaḥ
english: Then the unsurpassed milk of the Kṛttikās welled forth, and he, becoming six-faced to match the six of them, drank the milk from their breasts.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā kṣīram ekāhnā sukumāra vapus tadā ajayat svena vīryeṇa daityasainyagaṇān vibhuḥ
english: Having drunk the milk in a single day, that tender-bodied all-pervading one then conquered by his own valour the hosts of Daitya armies.

sanskrit: surasenāgaṇapatiṃ tatas tam amaladyutim abhyaṣiñcan suragaṇāḥ sametyāgnipurogamāḥ
english: Then the hosts of gods, gathering together led by Agni, consecrated him of spotless radiance as lord of the divine army.

sanskrit: eṣa te rāma gaṅgāyā vistaro 'bhihito mayā kumārasaṃbhavaś caiva dhanyaḥ puṇyas tathaiva ca
english: "This, Rāma, is the full account of Gaṅgā that has been set forth by me — and likewise the birth of the Prince, which is meritorious and sacred."
